title: Gate the 'northwind-shop-prod' cloud deployment before it ships
situation: The cloud team wants to deploy the production online shop from an infrastructure-as-code plan with 11 resources. Before it goes live, every resource must pass the security checks: no admin ports open to the internet, no public storage or databases, encryption on, and no over-powered permissions. One permission policy for the build pipeline grants full access to everything.
your_task: Scan all 11 resources in the plan against the security checks.
Record each failed check with its severity and the fix.
Deny any resource type that has no reviewed checks.
Make the deploy decision using the gate rules: any critical finding, or more high findings than allowed, blocks the release.
why_it_matters: One open admin port or public database can be found by attackers within hours. A build-pipeline account with full access means anyone who steals that pipeline can control the whole cloud account.
done_when: All 11 resources show PASS or FAIL with the checks that failed.
The gate decision is BLOCK, with the 5 critical and 3 high findings listed.
The wildcard IAM policy (iam-ci-deployer) is sent to the IAM team to be rewritten with only the actions and resources the deployer needs.

glossary.IaC (infrastructure as code): Defining servers, networks and permissions in files, so they can be reviewed before they are built.
glossary.Security group: A cloud firewall that controls which traffic can reach a resource.
glossary.IAM policy: A rule in Identity and Access Management that says which actions an account may take on which resources.
glossary.Least privilege: Giving an account only the access it needs, nothing more.
glossary.Availability zone: A separate data centre within a cloud region; using two keeps a service up if one fails.
glossary.Shared responsibility model: The split of security duties between the cloud provider and the customer.

talking_point: Scanned an 11-resource infrastructure-as-code plan, passed 3 resources and failed 8, and blocked the release on 5 critical and 3 high findings, including a build-pipeline (CI, continuous integration) deployer IAM policy that allowed every action on every resource.
